Bodanapally Bachi Reddy, Koratikal V, ... vs The State Of A.P.,
Rep. By P.P., ... on 16 April, 2024
 1
 The Honourable Sri Justice K.Surender
 Criminal Revision Case No.1683 Of 2009
Judgment:

entities.text: Koratikal V, ... vs The State Of A.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
This Criminal Revision Case is filed by the petitioner aggrieved by the judgment dated 30.09.2009 in Crl.A.No.18 of 2008, on the file of Family Judge-Cum-Additional Sessions Judge, Nalgonda,
confirming the judgment passed by the Judicial First Class Magistrate, Devarakonda vide order dated 30.01.2008 in C.C.No.76 of 2003.

2. Heard the learned counsel for the revision petitioner and learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing for respondent-State.
3.
The revision petitioner/accused was convicted for the offence under Section 420 of IPC.

The case against the revision petitioner is that a complaint was filed by the de-facto complainant/P.W.3 stating that the accused had taken an amount of Rs.3,05,000/- on 12.10.2002 from the complainant for supply of fish at Dindi village.
However, accused failed to supply the said fish.
Having failed to supply the fish, when questioned, he also refused to return the money given as advance.

Thereafter,
on enquiry, the de-facto complainant came to know that the accused had cheated other persons also in the very same manner inducing them of supplying fish and taking advance.
Neither the fish was supplied nor the money was returned.
4. The Police having received the complaint from the de-facto complainant/P.W.3 investigated the case and filed charge sheet under Section 420 of IPC.
During the course of examination, the complainant examined himself as P.W.3 and two others witnesses were examined as P.W.4 and P.W.5.
There was an agreement also which was entered into with P.W.3 to P.W.5 which were marked as Exs.P.3 to P.5.
From the evidence on record, the learned Magistrate found that the accused had deliberately taken the amount having knowledge that he was not in a position to deliver the fish as promised.

For the said reason of deliberately cheating the victims P.W.3 to P.W.5,
conviction was recorded under Section 420 of IPC.
5.

In the appeal, learned Sessions Judge found that the petitioner had in fact entered into agreement of supplying the fish which were marked as Exs.P.3 to P.5, having induced P.W.3 to P.W.5 and accordingly confirmed the findings of the learned Magistrate.
6. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the accused would submit that the accused was the member of the Society.
In fact, Society members were collecting the amount for the purpose of supplying fish.

However, though it was to the knowledge of the members of the Society that the Bodanapally Bachi Reddy, Koratikal V, ... vs The State Of A.P., Rep. By P.P., ... on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43050895/
1 amount was collected, no efforts were made to supply fish.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said circumstances, it cannot be said that the accused had cheated P.W.3 to P.W.5.
At most, it is the case of breach of contract and only civil liability would arise.
In fact, the witnesses should have approached the Civil Court seeking damages and to recover the amount.
No offence is made out under Section 420 of IPC, for which reason, the Revision has to be allowed.

7. To attract an offence under Section 420 of IPC, necessary ingredients which have to established by the prosecution are that there has to be deliberate misrepresentation, pursuant to which, the person who was induced by misrepresentation suffered by delivering property believing the said misrepresentation.
In the present case, it is apparent that the accused was not competent to supply fish, however, he collected amounts from P.W.3 to P.W.5 and entered into agreements for the purpose of supplying fish.

In the absence of supply of fish, the duty is cast upon the accused to return the said money in the background of his claim that he was part of the Society and he was authorized to receive the amounts.
8. The investigation does not reveal that the accused was the member of the Society.
The accused also did not make any endeavour to examine witnesses from the Society to show that he is part of the Society.
Accused collected amounts and the Society is responsible for supply of fish.

In the absence of any such evidence being adduced, considering the evidence of P.W.3 to P.W.5, it can be concluded that the accused had intention of cheating P.W.3 to P.W.5 from the inception of the transactions.
9. I do not find any grounds to set aside the findings of the Courts below.

10. However, the transactions are of the year, 2002 and nearly 22 years have passed by and according to the counsel, petitioner was in jail when the crime was registered and subsequently when the revision was filed.
On instructions, learned Additional Public Prosecutor submits that there are no criminal antecedents against the accused.
11. For the above said reasons, this Court deems it appropriate to reduce the sentence of imprisonment to the period already undergone.
12. Accordingly, the Criminal Revision Case is partly allowed reducing the sentence of the imprisonment imposed on the petitioner to the period already undergone.
Miscellaneous applications pending, if any, shall stand closed.

K.SURENDER, J Date: 16.04.2024 dv THE HONOURABLE SRI JUSTICE K.SURENDER CRIMINAL REVISION CASE No.1683 OF 2009 Dt. 16.04.2024 dv Bodanapally Bachi Reddy, Koratikal V, ... vs The State Of A.P., Rep. By P.P., ... on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43050895/
